problems: The element is inactive in PC-3 and enhancer- or promoter-like in 0 of 170 core biosamples (E05), so none of these chains currently has evidence that this cCRE functions as an enhancer in the stated prostate context.
The gene links remain candidate-level: RFX6 has strong L2G support and is nearby, but E06 provides no cCRE-to-RFX6 perturbation or contact evidence.

All TF binding claims rely on in-vitro QBiC-SELEX predictions. For H2–H5 the predicted stronger binding is to C, the prostate-cancer-associated allele; H1 predicts stronger binding to T. No allele-specific transcriptional effect or gene-expression direction in prostate cells is established, so binding direction alone cannot explain disease risk.

The new PC-3 ChIP lookups do not establish a causal TF mechanism: E25 reports an AR peak containing the variant with a summit 99 bp away, while E26 and E27 are marked not tested and should not be treated as negative results.

checks.why: Tests whether the reported AR summit is supported by a variant-containing AR peak in the specific prostate line where the cCRE was called inactive.
Tests for a variant-containing GATA2 peak in the same prostate line, helping compare the strongest alt-binding candidates in the relevant biosample.
Checks whether the reported nearby HOXB13 summit is supported by a variant-containing peak in PC-3, relevant to the competing ref-binding hypothesis.

critique.next_experiment: First identify a prostate-relevant model in which EH38E2496909 is active. In that model, compare endogenous T and C alleles by allele-specific TF occupancy and expression of candidate targets, then perturb the implicated TF and CRISPRi the cCRE to test whether occupancy and any allele-dependent expression effect require that element.

lookups.why: Tests whether the reported AR summit is supported by a variant-containing AR peak in the specific prostate line where the cCRE was called inactive.
Tests for a variant-containing GATA2 peak in the same prostate line, helping compare the strongest alt-binding candidates in the relevant biosample.
Checks whether the reported nearby HOXB13 summit is supported by a variant-containing peak in PC-3, relevant to the competing ref-binding hypothesis.

games.reason: HOXB13 has stronger matched-context support: it is more highly expressed and has a closer ChIP-seq summit (11 bp versus VDR’s 38 bp). Its QBiC-SELEX model also predicts a substantially stronger ref-over-alt binding difference than VDR’s alt-over-ref prediction. The other chain links are shared, and the HOXB13 result not being tested in PC-3 does not count against it.

HOXB13 is better supported as the acting TF: it is substantially more highly expressed in the matched context and has the closer ChIP-seq summit (125.7 TPM, 11 bp) than VDR (4.4 TPM, 38 bp). Both chains have an allele-specific in-vitro binding prediction in the stated direction, and both share the same inactive-element and target-gene limitations. The HOXB13 not-tested result does not count against it.
